# Pre-Market Briefing

## 1. Market Tone
- **Confirmed:** Friday’s tape was mixed-to-soft, with the **Nasdaq** down **0.64%** while the **S&P 500** was basically flat at **+0.05%** and the **Dow** up **0.46%** (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** The email frames the current mood as **AI spending skepticism**, after Alphabet’s capex-related miss and weaker AI-linked free cash flow trends weighed on megacaps (The Motley Fool).
- **Interpretation:** Risk appetite looks fragile in large-cap growth/AI names, but morning futures were described as firmer after crude eased (The Motley Fool). That could support a bounce in broader indices if tech stabilizes.

## 2. Macro And Calendar
- **Confirmed:** The **Federal Reserve** meets **Wednesday at 2:00pm ET**; the email says CME FedWatch showed about a **one-third probability of a rate rise this time** and “up to three quarters” by the September 16 meeting (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** **Crude oil futures** were said to be down around **5%**, with WTI back to around **$84/barrel** after a pause in U.S.-Iran conflict (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** Futures were reportedly up pre-open: **S&P 500 futures** close to **+1%** and **Nasdaq futures** over **+1.5%** this morning (The Motley Fool).
- **Unclear:** No other economic calendar items were provided.

## 3. Earnings And Company News
- **Today after the close:** **SUI** reports Q2 results; management had raised full-year expectations after Q1 (The Motley Fool).
- **Tuesday after the close:** **V** reports Q3 results; management expects Q3 revenue to be the lowest quarter of the fiscal year (The Motley Fool).
- **Wednesday after the close:** **MSFT** reports Q4 earnings; Azure commercial cloud platform growth hit 40% in Q3, and AI capex will be watched closely (The Motley Fool).
- **Wednesday after the close:** **META** reports Q2; analysts expect about **$60.2B** in revenue, and the market is watching reported Anthropic-related compute leasing talks (The Motley Fool).
- **Wednesday after the close:** **SBUX** reports Q3; investors are watching Brian Niccol’s turnaround plan after a return to global sales growth in Q2 (The Motley Fool).
- **Thursday afternoon:** **AMZN** reports Q2; analysts expect revenue growth of **16% to 19% YoY** (The Motley Fool).
- **Thursday after the close:** **AAPL** reports Q3; revenue expectations are cited at **$108.0B to $108.8B**, with its OpenAI lawsuit in focus (The Motley Fool).
- **Thursday before the open:** **MA** reports Q3 (The Motley Fool).

## 4. Top Movers And Catalysts
- **Confirmed catalyst:** **NVDA** is reportedly in talks to provide guarantees for OpenAI tied to a massive data-center/energy project; the WSJ-reported financial backstop is said to be worth **$250B** (The Motley Fool citing WSJ).
- **Confirmed catalyst:** **AVGO** reportedly inked a **$200B+** AI-related deal with Samsung covering HBM supply, advanced manufacturing, and packaging (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed theme:** The market is reacting to AI spending concerns after **GOOG** and **TSLA** showed negative quarterly free cash flow and pressured the Nasdaq last week (The Motley Fool).
- **Interpretation:** **NVDA**, **AVGO**, and the rest of the AI hardware complex may see pre-market attention; reaction likely depends on whether traders view these deals as demand confirmation or more capex/financing risk.

## 5. Ranked Buy Candidates
1. **AVGO**
   - **Catalyst:** Reported deal worth over **$200B** with Samsung for HBM, 2nm-and-below manufacturing, and advanced packaging (The Motley Fool).
   - **Why it might matter for a swing:** It could reinforce the AI supply-chain theme and support follow-through if the market sees it as tangible demand validation.
   - **What would invalidate it:** If the market treats the deal as too vague, too long-dated, or already priced in; also invalid if broad AI-capex skepticism overwhelms the news.
   - **Must check before entry:** Pre-market gap size, whether price holds above the opening range, and whether the move is broadening beyond AVGO into semis.

2. **NVDA**
   - **Catalyst:** Reportedly in talks to provide guarantees for OpenAI in a large data-center project; financing discussions are ongoing (The Motley Fool citing WSJ).
   - **Why it might matter for a swing:** Could reassert NVDA’s central role in AI infrastructure demand and trigger a momentum move if traders focus on scale rather than financing risk.
   - **What would invalidate it:** If the market views the guarantee as balance-sheet risk, or if the stock fades after the open and fails to hold the gap.
   - **Must check before entry:** Whether the report is confirmed by additional outlets, whether the open holds, and whether semis/AI peers are confirming.

3. **MSFT**
   - **Catalyst:** Earnings Wednesday after the close; Azure commercial cloud growth was 40% in Q3, and AI capex is the key watch item (The Motley Fool).
   - **Why it might matter for a swing:** A strong report could restore confidence in hyperscaler AI spending if investors want proof that large capex is converting into cloud growth.
   - **What would invalidate it:** Any sign that capex is rising faster than monetization, or disappointing Azure guidance.
   - **Must check before entry:** Price action into earnings, options-implied move, and whether the stock is extended ahead of the print.

4. **META**
   - **Catalyst:** Earnings Wednesday after the close; revenue expected around **$60.2B**, plus reported Anthropic compute-leasing talks (The Motley Fool).
   - **Why it might matter for a swing:** A clean print or strong AI monetization commentary could support a post-earnings continuation move.
   - **What would invalidate it:** Any indication that AI spending is weighing on margins without offsetting revenue growth.
   - **Must check before entry:** How the stock trades versus the broader megacap group and whether the reported Anthropic deal is treated as material.

## 6. Swing Setup Board

| **AVGO** | Catalyst Continuation | AI supply-chain reaction to Samsung deal | Hold above opening range / gap support after the open | Lose opening range or fade back through gap support | Prior swing high / measured move from gap, if momentum persists | Keep size modest; news may be priced quickly | Gap is huge and fades immediately, or semis do not confirm |

| **MSFT** | Risk Watch | Earnings setup with AI-capex scrutiny | Only actionable if post-earnings trend forms on volume | Earnings gap reversal / loss of first support | If earnings gap holds, look for continuation toward next resistance | Do not front-run blindly; event risk is high | Reaction is mixed or the stock gaps without trend follow-through |
| **META** | Risk Watch | Earnings setup with AI and revenue focus | Only if report produces clean post-earnings expansion | Loss of post-earnings opening support | Hold-and-go continuation if volume confirms | Avoid size ahead of the print | Move is noisy or guided lower without reclaim |

## 7. Setup Watch
- **Breakout / Momentum:** **AVGO** if the Samsung deal drives a clean gap-and-go and semis confirm.
- **Catalyst Continuation:** **NVDA** if the OpenAI financing report is validated and the stock holds the gap.
- **Risk Watch:** **MSFT**, **META**, **AMZN**, **AAPL**, **SBUX**, **V**, **MA** heading into a dense earnings week.
- **Trend Pullback:** None clearly actionable from the provided material alone.
- **Reversal Bounce:** No strong reversal setup is supported by the source material alone.

## 8. Risk Watch
- **Confirmed:** AI capex skepticism is the dominant risk theme; that can hit megacaps and semis even on good news (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** **GOOG** and **TSLA** showed negative free cash flow and were part of last week’s Nasdaq weakness (The Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** The Fed decision is midweek, adding event risk for index and sector rotations (The Motley Fool).
- **Interpretation:** Pre-earnings megacaps may be vulnerable to “buy the rumor, sell the news” behavior if expectations are too high.

## 9. Sector And Theme Watch
- **AI / Semiconductors:** **NVDA**, **AVGO**, and the broader AI hardware chain are in focus on large-deal headlines.
- **Megacap Cloud / Platforms:** **MSFT**, **META**, **AMZN**, **AAPL** all face the same broad question: whether AI spend is translating into durable revenue.
- **Payments:** **V** and **MA** may trade on consumer/payment-volume commentary, though no major catalyst was provided beyond earnings.
- **REITs / Income:** **SUI** is a lower-volatility earnings name with dividend context, but the material is not strong enough for a trade idea by itself.
- **Energy:** Lower crude may ease broader inflation pressure, but no direct trade setup was provided.

## 10. Worth Reading
- “**Big Tech Faces Test After Alphabet’s Miss Last Week**” — useful for the broader megacap/AI spending frame (The Motley Fool).
- “**Report: Nvidia and Broadcom Ink Big AI Deals**” — the most relevant catalyst article for pre-market trade research (The Motley Fool).
- “**Fed Set to Meet Amid Choppy Markets**” — relevant for macro/event risk into Wednesday (The Motley Fool).

## 11. Open Questions
- Will the market treat the **NVDA** and **AVGO** headlines as genuine demand confirmation, or as more evidence of expensive AI capex?
- Can **MSFT** and **META** show enough AI monetization to offset spending concerns?
- Will the Fed meeting reinforce or reduce the current risk-on/risk-off tug of war?
- Are the reported deals and financing talks already priced in at the open?

## Notable Noise
- **SUI**, **SBUX**, **V**, **MA**, **AMZN**, and **AAPL** are important earnings names, but the source material is too limited to make a high-confidence swing call before additional price/volume checks.
- The SpaceX IPO discussion is interesting, but it is not an actionable pre-market setup from the provided material.
